title: Q3 Townhall orchestration checklist and ownership matrix (v0.1)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working orchestration checklist + ownership matrix for the Q3 all-company townhall. Goal is to produce a 60–75 minute session that: 1) demonstrates progress against company OKRs, 2) surfaces priorities and constraints for Q3, and 3) leaves engineers and product teams with clear next steps and owners.

Audience:
- All employees (cross-functional)
- Execs and managers will present sections; ICs encouraged to attend and engage on breakout Q&A.

Tone and constraints (guidance for presenters):
- Transparent about trade-offs (cost/latency/reliability) but avoid deep technical digs beyond 1–2 slides per team.
- Timebox exec updates (max 6 minutes each).
- Use concrete outcomes (metrics + one-paragraph summary) rather than long narratives.

High-level schedule draft (60–75 minutes):
- 00:00–00:05: Welcome + one-line company health metric (CEO)
- 00:05–00:15: State of product and slides on adoption/throughput/costs (Head of Product)
- 00:15–00:30: Engineering update: serving runtime improvements + incidents and reliability plan (CTO/Head of Eng)
- 00:30–00:40: Customer momentum & enterprise asks (Head of GTM/CS)
- 00:40–00:50: Dedicated & Private deployment roadmap and compliance highlights (VP of Sales / Head of Private)
- 00:50–01:00: Key OKR review and what success looks like for Q3 (Ops/Product)
- 01:00–01:10: Live Q&A (moderated) + breakouts for product/eng deep-dive rooms
- 01:10–01:15: Closing + immediate asks for next 2 weeks

Primary deliverables and owners (ownership matrix):
- Full slide deck (single Google Slides doc, final by 2026-03-25): Owner = Priya Desai; Support = Jonah Kim, Marcus Liu
- One-line company health stat and visual (data team chart + notes): Owner = Marcus Liu; Support = Observability
- Engineering incident summary + SLA remediation timeline (1 slide): Owner = Jonah Kim; Support = SRE team
- Customer story + 1 pager for GTM: Owner = Sophie Green; Support = CS leads
- OKR summary slide + 3 measurable takeaways: Owner = Elena Park; Support = Product Ops and PMs
- Moderator and Q&A script (with escalation cues): Owner = Elena Park; Support = Exec Office

Orchestration checklist (tick boxes for runbook):
- [ ] Confirm venue/logistics and streaming link (Ops) — deadline 2026-03-22
- [ ] Slides assigned and first draft uploaded to shared deck — deadline 2026-03-18
- [ ] Slide review session with execs (dry run 1) — scheduled 2026-03-24
- [ ] Dry run 2 (full timed run) — scheduled 2026-03-29
- [ ] Breakout rooms and leads confirmed — deadline 2026-03-27
- [ ] Pre-event comms to company (what to expect + suggested prep) — Owner: Comms — send 2026-03-30
- [ ] Post-event feedback survey drafted — Owner: People Ops — ready by event end

OKR draft to present (working language + metric targets):
- Objective A: Make Redwood the predictable inference platform of choice for scale customers.
  - KR1: Reduce 95th percentile tokenize latency by 20% on the hosted API across top 3 models (baseline Apr 2026). Owner: Eng-Serving-Runtime
  - KR2: Increase Dedicated renewal pipeline coverage to $MM (placeholder) and close 6 new reserved contracts by EOY. Owner: Sales-Dedicated
  - KR3: Ship private deployment reference architecture (VPC/on-prem) and complete two pilot installs. Owner: Private-Deployments
- Objective B: Lower unit inference costs for mid-market customers.
  - KR1: Deliver automated quantization profile suggestions and reduce per-token cost by 15% for targeted workloads. Owner: Optimize
  - KR2: Launch cost-visibility tooling into Console and onboard 50 customers to beta. Owner: Console-and-Tooling

Presenter briefing notes (short bullets to hand to speakers):
- Start with the metric — why the audience should care.
- One slide = one message. Visuals over dense text.
- If discussing regressions, state root cause and one-sentence mitigation plan.
- Highlight cross-team dependencies and clear asks at the end (who needs to act, by when).

Ask sequencing (immediate post-townhall asks for managers):
1) Reinforce OKR priorities in team standups (within 48 hours). Owner: Managers
2) Triage backlog items that block KR deliverables (72 hours). Owner: Team Leads
3) Reach out to customer pilots that align with Private roadmap (1 week). Owner: Solutions Eng

Escalation contacts (tactical):
- Incident/escalation for live event streaming: SRE on-call (pager), backup webcast: Ops team
- Last-minute slide/asset issues (day of): Priya Desai (content owner) and Elena Park (run-of-show)

Risks & mitigations (short list):
- Risk: Slides overrun and we lose Q&A time. Mitigation: enforce strict dry run cutoffs; allocate a Q&A queue to Slack thread for follow-up.
- Risk: Execs diverge into deep technical discussions. Mitigation: designate 2 breakout rooms and redirect deep questions there; moderator to intervene.
- Risk: Conflicting messages on product priorities. Mitigation: product ops to consolidate three unified bullets and circulate 48 hours before event.

Open questions for the team (items to resolve before first draft review):
- Do we want a customer panel (live) or recorded customer story? (Pros/cons: live = more energy but riskier)
- Which single company health metric best captures momentum without oversimplifying? (growth of host requests vs. revenue vs. uptime)
- Are we comfortable publishing a preliminary Dedicated ARR target in the slide deck, or should that stay for sales-only channels?

Next milestones (short timeline):
- 2026-03-18: All first-draft slides in deck (owners must upload)
- 2026-03-22: Internal content freeze for factual/metric edits
- 2026-03-24: Exec dry run 1 (feedback round)
- 2026-03-29: Full timed dry run 2
- 2026-04-01: Final deck published and all pre-reads sent
- 2026-04-05: Townhall event (target date)

Notes to collaborators: keep language plain, avoid marketing hyperbole in the OKR slides, and use consistent metric baselines (call out date windows). Add any linked Jira keys or Confluence pages into the deck notes so PMs can click through.

Quick contact list:
- Elena Park (owner, product ops) — elena.park@redwood.ai
- Priya Desai (slides/content) — priya.desai@redwood.ai
- Jonah Kim (eng updates + SRE liaison) — jonah.kim@redwood.ai
- Marcus Liu (data/metrics) — marcus.liu@redwood.ai
- Sophie Green (customer stories/CS) — sophie.green@redwood.ai

This is intentionally a living doc — expect iteration after slide review. Mark changes with initials and date in the shared deck notes.
